transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because lately, after a long shift or when I’m done studying, I end up eating way more than I mean to. Like I’ll have a whole fast-food meal, then snacks and whatever’s in the fridge, all in one sitting.
After one of these episodes of overeating, do you ever try to 'undo' it—like making yourself throw up, using laxatives, fasting afterward, or exercising a lot to compensate?
Sometimes, yeah. I’ll go to the bathroom and make myself throw up. Other times I take laxatives. I get scared about what all that food is going to do to me.

latest_inference.note: Patient confirmed compensatory behaviors (self-induced vomiting, laxative use) following binge eating episodes, which is diagnostic for bulimia nervosa. This rules out F50.8 (atypical/other eating disorder, which lacks the classic binge-purge pattern) and E66.9 (obesity, as there's no mention of elevated weight/BMI and the compensatory behaviors point away from simple overeating/obesity).

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports recurrent episodes of binge eating (rapid consumption of large amounts of food in one sitting, felt to be excessive/uncontrolled) after stress triggers (long shifts, studying), followed by compensatory behaviors including self-induced vomiting and laxative use, driven by fear of weight gain/consequences of the food intake. This pattern of binge-purge cycles is consistent with Bulimia Nervosa (F50.2) rather than an unspecified eating disorder, given the clear presence of both binge eating and compensatory purging behaviors.

confirmed_symptoms: Eating an objectively large amount of food in a discrete period (fast-food meal plus snacks and additional food)
Sense of overeating beyond intention ('eat way more than I mean to')
Episodes triggered by stress (after long shifts or studying)
Use of laxatives to compensate for food intake
Fear/anxiety about the physical consequences of the food consumed

additional_requirements: Presence of both binge eating and recurrent compensatory purging behaviors (vomiting, laxative use) confirmed
Fear of weight/body consequences related to eating confirmed
